refactor_acceptance.criteria: Implement source parity or explicit user requirements, inspect existing solutions before adding code, review and consolidate confirmed duplication through focused tasks, and use the simplest design preserving correctness, identity, durability and recovery. conversation_api.replay: GET /v1/projects/{project}/conversations/{conversation}/events?after={sequence}&limit={1..1000}; default after 0 and limit 100; page also limited to 4 MiB of stored event JSON. Continue from last returned sequence, including after a short byte-limited page.
conversation_api.stream: GET /v1/projects/{project}/conversations/{conversation}/stream?after={event_sequence}&after_commands={command_revision}; coder/websocket, read-only. Initial {type:ready,version:1,conversation_id,after,after_commands}; transcript frames {type:event,version:1,event:{id,conversation_id,sequence,event,created_at}}; command frames {type:command,version:1,command:{id,revision,sequence,command,request_id,target_instance_id,state,created_at,updated_at,conversation_id}}. Persist event sequence and command revision separately for reconnect. Command frames carry latest committed snapshots and may repeat one command across multiple revisions; a repeated snapshot is never new execution intent. Clients must allow at least 5 MiB inbound messages. Idle connections are pinged and streams drain on shutdown. Ready also includes owner; subsequent {type:owner,version:1,owner} frames announce instance transfer. Workers must stop if the owner differs from their bound origin.

commands.enqueue: POST /v1/projects/{project}/conversations/{conversation}/commands with {id: UUID, command:{kind,text?,permission_event_id?,option_id?,prompt_command_id?}}. Bearer-authenticated UI clients may enqueue without worker origin headers. Retry with identical ID/content returns the original record; changed content conflicts. Encoded command limit 1 MiB. Prompt and control backlogs each allow up to 128 nonterminal commands.
commands.kinds: prompt requires nonempty text; permission references the exact persisted permission event UUID and an offered option ID (empty option cancels); cancel references the claimed prompt command UUID. Permission/cancel intent is checked at enqueue and dispatch so delayed controls cannot target a later prompt or reused RPC ID.
commands.list: GET /v1/projects/{project}/conversations/{conversation}/commands?after={command_sequence}&limit={1..1000}. Default after 0/limit 100. This lists intent with current state; command sequences do not advance on state changes.
commands.changes: GET /v1/projects/{project}/conversations/{conversation}/commands/changes?after={revision}&limit={1..1000}. Transactional change records deliver latest committed snapshots, not historical state at each revision. Revisions are monotonic and may have gaps per conversation. A page is also byte-bounded.
commands.claim: POST /v1/projects/{project}/conversations/{conversation}/commands/{id}/claim with complete current worker origin headers. Idempotent claim. Only one prompt may be claimed, in FIFO order. Permission/cancel controls are independent from prompt backlog; expired controls return a rejected record without dispatch.
commands.result: POST /v1/projects/{project}/conversations/{conversation}/commands/{id}/result with {state:done|rejected|interrupted} and current worker origin headers. Requires claimed state; terminal result retries must agree.
commands.handoff: Instance replacement interrupts claimed work and queued controls. Unclaimed prompts transfer to the replacement instance. Interrupted commands require explicit reconciliation; do not automatically resend a potentially executed prompt.

worker_runtime.new_run: amux worker run --state PATH --server URL --project IDENT --task UUID --directory CHECKOUT [--prompt TEXT]. Requires GATEWAY_API_KEY or --api-key-env. Default provider command is agy acp --stdio. Select --provider codex for the native Codex adapter; its default command is codex app-server --listen stdio://. --provider claude selects native Claude stream-json with host permission routing.
worker_runtime.resume: amux worker run --state PATH --run-id UUID. Uses saved gateway/project/conversation/native session/directory/command; creation flags cannot silently replace the saved run. The run ID and conversation ID are printed before execution. A saved provider is authoritative; explicitly supplying a different --provider on resume is rejected.
worker_runtime.native_command: Optional --agent-command is a JSON string array for a configured native stdio executable and its arguments. It is saved with the run and executed directly without a shell or PTY. Provider credentials come from the process environment/provider configuration, not an automatic login flow.
worker_runtime.ownership: CLI holds the local journal profile OS lock for its lifetime; the shared Store also rejects duplicate in-process engines for one run. Provider-neutral worker callers must exclusively own the journal profile across processes.
worker_runtime.recovery: Drain the ordered old-instance outbox before ownership transfer. Persist a planned instance UUID before remote compare-and-swap so a lost resume response can retry the same identity. Activate locally after remote confirmation; never replay locally started commands. Resume the exact saved native provider session or fail.
worker_runtime.publication: Provider callbacks commit locally before network publication. Native session binding precedes events; events and command results share one ordered durable outbox. Publication retries reuse event UUIDs, and local acknowledgement only removes the current head. Event cursor and command revision are persisted independently.
worker_runtime.commands: The worker commits command snapshots and revisions atomically, claims remotely, journals started before provider invocation, then queues the terminal result locally. Controls verify current local permission event UUIDs and active prompt IDs. Input is recorded independently from provider echo behavior. Prompt failures are interrupted rather than presumed safe to replay.
worker_runtime.network: Transient HTTP/stream failures retry with bounded backoff. A disconnected UI or gateway does not stop a running provider; output remains local until publication resumes. Fatal authorization/ownership conflicts stop the worker without dropping its outbox. Conversation streams announce ownership so a connected stale worker retires its provider.
worker_runtime.scope_limit: Selected-conversation and native pool runtimes share one provider engine. Pools now handle ordinary tick assignments; secure peers, full session/delegation scheduling, project discovery, MCP tools, desktop parity and packaging remain unfinished.

plugin_bus_contract.access: Store.EventBus() exposes the shared in-process bus. Subscribe(buffer) returns a subscription with receive-only C channel; call Unsubscribe when finished. Publish fans out to independent subscribers, not competing workers on one shared receive channel.
plugin_bus_contract.events: Lightweight value events carry Topic and At: project_changed, task_changed, conversation_changed, presence_changed, router_changed and tick. These are reconciliation notifications, not durable business-event payloads.
plugin_bus_contract.ordering: Task/conversation notifications publish after commit. Consumers acquire subscriptions before querying authoritative storage. Existing coalesced TaskEventChanges/ConversationChanges APIs remain intact for compatible streams and worker outboxes.
plugin_bus_contract.overflow: Bounded subscription queues never block committed mutations. Overflow closes only that subscription with ErrSlowConsumer; drain/resubscribe and reconcile durable state. Bus close reports ErrBusClosed. Channel lifecycle and fanout are race-tested.
plugin_bus_contract.clock: Server runtime owns a time.Ticker with the Rust-compatible 30-second default. Missed ticks are skipped; cancellation stops the ticker and shutdown joins it. A short interval drives lifecycle tests without a 30-second sleep.
plugin_bus_contract.review: Production completions are drained through task.completed deliveries and the review plugin. Old task_review_outbox rows bridge atomically to durable events with review subscription checks, while passive library handlers retain existing default behavior.
plugin_bus_contract.not_parity: Complete builtin router wiring now runs in the headless server; full application parity is still incomplete, including secure peers, remaining bundled MCP tools, channel adapters and desktop features.

worker_pool_runtime.create: amux worker pool --state PATH --server URL --project IDENT --directory PATH [--provider antigravity|codex|claude] [--slots 1..32] [--agent-command JSON-array]. Credential runtime-only through API key environment. Local profile lock spans all slots and provider lifetimes.
worker_pool_runtime.resume: amux worker pool --state PATH --pool-id UUID. Pool config and stable per-slot session, current instance, active run and presence sequence persist in SQLite. Active runs resume before adopting new work. No silent provider/config replacement.
worker_pool_runtime.adoption: POST /v1/projects/{project}/worker-assignment with {} and exact agent origin headers. Returns null when no exactly owned in_progress task. Atomically creates {run_id,task,conversation} with one queued initial prompt or replays the existing binding with the same run, conversation, and prompt IDs. Replay requires an exact conversation owner origin match and, when the conversation has a recorded principal, the same authenticated enrolled-client principal. Legacy conversations without a recorded principal retain origin-only replay eligibility. Adoption ownership failures return HTTP 403. Binding invalidates when task status changes, retaining prior conversations/history so new claims have fresh intent. X-Task-Goal must match a tagged task before creating or returning its binding. Missing or wrong selection is HTTP 409.
worker_pool_runtime.recovery: Conversation resume transfers a task owner only if its in_progress owner exactly equals the previous conversation origin. Task ownership, conversation handoff and command interruption commit together. Foreign and terminal task owners remain untouched. Pending native instance CAS is accounted for during runtime ownership checks.
worker_pool_runtime.execution: Shared worker.Run handles each slot conversation. Prompt turn completion does not mark task done. Slot is released locally only after task workflow no longer considers it active, owned worker has stopped/joined and pending output is flushed. Heartbeat/network loss alone never releases potentially running work.

review_scheduling.ranking: Completion review labels freeze the preferred provider and contributor exclusions. Preference compares provider mismatch first, then prior contributor. Legacy reviews without a provider label derive the opposite provider from the source owner or latest agent comment. Preferences can fall back; they are not permanent exclusion barriers.
review_scheduling.manual_claims: A new claim yields only to a better-ranked eligible ready reviewer in the same project. Busy/drafting/unknown/expired/wrong-OS/foreign-project peers do not block fallback. Liveness uses max(server wall time,persisted presence clock), so an expired peer cannot block between ticks. Existing exact-owner in_progress retries remain valid when a better peer arrives.
review_scheduling.ticks: Atomic allocator persists per-project ordinary/review turn preference. A successful ordinary allocation prefers queued reviews next, a successful review returns ordinary preference. Ready peers are removed as claims commit inside the same transaction. Codex ordinary-first and FIFO eligibility remain. Turn preference rolls back with failed allocation batch.
review_scheduling.fresh_context: Automatic nonideal reviewer fallback requires presence.review_context_clear=true. Migration12 adds a false default for existing/old clients. Native pools advertise true because each new task adoption creates a new conversation/run and starts an unbound native provider session; resuming the same active task retains its own session. Historical gone presence rows are excluded from readiness.

task_reorder.route: POST /v1/projects/{ident}/tasks/reorder?status=todo|in_progress|stalled|user_review|done with order array and optional moved_task_id, returns bare fresh task summary array. moved_task_id names the single task allowed to cross status into the target column; omitting it permits rank-only reorders, and any listed row whose status differs returns 409 so the board refreshes. stalled is rank-only: tasks already stalled may be reordered, but crossings into stalled are rejected because the activity controller manages that status. Optional goal query or X-Task-Goal filters response. Duplicate status/goal fields rejected.
task_reorder.invariants: Rank-only changes preserve owner reservations. Column crossings share the ordinary workflow and transaction. Any listed task other than moved_task_id whose current status differs from the target column returns 409 ErrTaskConflict and rolls back the whole reorder, even when moved_task_id is supplied. Agent crossings away from in_progress require the changeset-aware PATCH workflow.

task_cancellation.state: One taskMutation transaction validates current state/owner, merges confirmed file paths, stores prior owner/session/start provenance, inserts immutable report, then writes cancelled status. Existing trigger emits task_cancelled after the merged paths are present; notifications publish after commit. History and owner fields remain. User-review/completed/dispatch/unbound-owned work is refused.
task_cancellation.replay: Already-cancelled replay succeeds only for identical full reporter origin and trimmed reason, before requiring a new changeset. It reuses timestamp/report without another lifecycle event. Conflicting replay fails; missing changeset creates no guided pending request. Cancelled tasks only transition to done through existing lifecycle rules.
task_cancellation.stopping: executor_stop_confirmed is always false. Recording cancellation is independent from observing provider-process termination. SDK requires explicit JSON false and validates reporter, prior claim consistency, current task state and scope.
task_cancellation.schema: Before migration14, startup widens recognized legacy three/four-status CHECK constraints on a pinned connection after a protected VACUUM INTO logical backup with a write-capable file sync and Unix directory syncing. Windows uses the SQLite VFS baseline without claiming POSIX directory-fsync guarantees; native Windows ACL/runtime verification remains pending. Table rebuild preserves rows, rowids, comments, indexes, triggers and references; foreign-key checking precedes commit and connection PRAGMAs are restored on success/failure. Unknown constraints and newer Go schemas fail closed. SQLite user_version is retained. Full exported Rust schema upgrade is tested for both historical CHECK variants, including all original schema objects and seeded review/execution/receipt/router history; broader application parity remains incomplete.

durable_plugin_runtime.entry: router.NewRuntime validates/copies plugins and policies; Runtime.Run owns one cancellable lifetime, independent bus subscription, bounded workers (default/cap64), startup recovery and token release. durable_plugin_runtime.execution: Ordered pre_exec/exec/post_exec; Continue advances, Stop ends phases and vetoes only declared dependents, Fail/panic retries from first step. Event bytes/correlation are copied for steps. StepContext.Emit sets plugin source and causing event correlation.
durable_plugin_runtime.scheduling: SQL claims use indexed FIFO heads across all event types plus paged parallel work; dependencies must complete before admission. Stopped/skipped/failed dependencies skip dependents, retries hold them. Retry delay is1s doubling through16s then30s; zero MaxAttempts retries forever, bounded policies terminally fail. First cap crossing transactionally emits router.retrying without recursion.
durable_plugin_runtime.durability: Running work resets for replay on acquisition; removed subscriptions skip unfinished deliveries, terminal failures retain history. Runtime token plus claimed failure-count snapshot fence stale completions; duplicate finish acknowledgements do not increment attempts twice. Completion recording errors retry only the cached result and pause new claims until acknowledged.
durable_plugin_runtime.lifetime: Subscribe before acquisition and reconcile startup/RouterChanged/tick/retry deadlines. Overflow resubscribes without resetting active work. Cancellation stops admission, joins owned cooperative steps and releases/inactivates the token, even if durable release cleanup fails.

durable_plugin_sources.drain: DrainRouterTaskOutbox selects oldest1..200 rows, validates known kinds/payloads and atomically emits events plus pending deliveries and deletes acknowledged outbox rows. durable_plugin_sources.clock: plugins.RunClockSource consumes the server-owned tick channel, emits clock.tick v1 from source clock with current at milliseconds, and owns no second ticker. No startup tick; bounded coalescing skips accumulated ticks, ignores other topics, drops failed emissions until the next tick, and resubscribes after overflow.

durable_plugin_presence.clock_plugin: PresencePlugin consumes clock.tick, client.heartbeat, client.activity and retained terminal.activity v1. All share one observation authority and monotonic clock; activity and heartbeat transitions, captured source cursors and causal event emission/ack commit atomically. Native captured heartbeat callbacks do not overwrite accepted native state.
durable_plugin_presence.source: RunPresenceSource shares the reviewed task source lifecycle, subscribing before startup drain and reconciling on PresenceChanged/tick with bounded batches, fixed retry deadlines, overflow recovery and cancellation. Clock reconciliation publishes both PresenceChanged and committed RouterChanged notifications; rows beyond its atomic200 batch retain their cause and drain promptly.
durable_plugin_presence.snapshot: LivePresence reads one clock/data SQL snapshot over canonical native and event observations, keeps the clock even when all rows are hidden by repository rebinding, and preserves typed routing metadata. Raw unknown/unresolved project identities remain observational; raw snapshots never gain native AutoAssign or review-context capabilities.
durable_plugin_presence.safety: Transition failures roll back report cursor/state or clock evaluation and emitted rows as appropriate. Native gone is liveness/omission, not executor-stop confirmation; active offline task ownership is unchanged. Presence plugin does not invoke assignment.
